description: Where this board's build finds its tools, and nothing else. Replaces the
old workflow config file, whose remaining live content was one key - the
path to kicad-cli - alongside configuration for a router this project no
Linux-native. KiCad is the distribution package, so kicad-cli and the
stock libraries sit on the system prefix and `pcbnew` imports from the
system interpreter's dist-packages - there is no separate bundled Python
to find. `cli` and `python` are bare command names on purpose: they
resolve through PATH, which keeps a fresh clone working on any machine
that has the packages, and the resolved absolute path is recorded in the
run's own provenance rather than frozen here.
Design rules, net classes, via sizes and clearances are deliberately NOT
restated here. They live in the .kicad_pro net classes, which is the same
source the generator, the router and the validator all read.

router.name: KiCad Routing Tools
router.development_checkout_note: Null on purpose. The router is a submodule of the toolkit at tooling/KiCadRoutingTools, pinned to a commit on its pcba-autonomy branch, so a recursive clone has it and no absolute path has to be true on more than one machine. This key survives as the development affordance it always was: set it to a local checkout to test an unpinned router, and pcbqa.krt will prefer it over the submodule. Setting it to a path that is not a KRT root is an error, never a silent fall-through.
router.note: Resolved through pcbqa.krt: explicit override, then PCB_KRT_PATH, then this development checkout, then the router vendored into the toolkit as its tooling/KiCadRoutingTools submodule, then a single active plugin installation; a path under disabled_pcm_plugins always refuses. On this machine it is the SUBMODULE that resolves, because development_checkout is null. The old PCM-rooted 'root' key is retired - that installation is disabled on purpose. plugin_dirs is the Linux KiCad user base, ~/.local/share/kicad, versioned; it need not exist, and while the submodule is present the scan is unreachable anyway, since a pinned router outranks an ambient installation. It stays declared so the order is complete and the disabled_pcm_plugins refusal has somewhere to apply.

toolkit.note: The pinned submodule. Board tools add this to sys.path through tools/_toolkit.py; no sibling checkout is ever used.
